newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pernod rises against weak bourse trend.
newsitem.headline: Pernod rises against weak bourse trend.

text.p: Shares in drinks company Pernod-Ricard SA rose on Tuesday on reports that UDF party representatives in the ruling conservative coalition were challenging a planned 17.1 percent tax increase on spirits.
The shares were up 1.52 percent at 273.10 francs at 1100 GMT while the bourse's CAC-40 index was down 1.2 percent.
Pernod shares had been hammered by the proposed tax increase, touching a year low of 266.10 francs last Friday.
The newspaper La Tribune said UDF representatives were pushing to trim the tax increase to 4.5 percent on spirits and raise taxes on beer and wine to make up the difference.
"These reports prompted a rebound but the company will suffer even if the rise is limited," one analyst said.
Pernod is more exposed to the effects of French taxes than champagne group LVMH and cognac company Remy Cointreau, which export a bigger proportion of their products.

Remy shares rose in early trading after the group reported a four percent rise in first-half sales. "That was a nice surprise," one trader said, noting that the biggest gains were in high-margin products that should help Remy's results.
But Remy shares gave up their early gains and were trading 0.80 franc lower at 125.70 at midday.
One trader said there was arbitrage on Tuesday between Pernod and LVMH shares. LVMH shares were down 1.5 percent at 1,116 francs.
